title: Sydney Home Prices Projected to Grow by 23% Over Three Years
content:
Sydney’s real estate market is set to experience a substantial upswing, with forecasts suggesting a remarkable 23% growth in home prices over the next three years. According to a recent report by Oxford Economics Australia, this surge is expected to be particularly pronounced in the unit market.


Sydney Home Prices Forecast: A 23% Growth Projection

The Residential Property Prospects report, which extends its property price and rental market predictions to 2026, indicates that the slow growth observed in Sydney’s home prices throughout the remainder of the 2024 financial year will be followed by accelerated growth in both FY25 and FY26.


Unit Prices to Outpace Houses: A Closer Look at the Projections

The report suggests that unit prices will outpace house prices, with an estimated growth of 23.4% compared to 15.8% for houses. If these predictions hold, Sydney’s median unit value could surpass the $1 million mark, reaching $1,029,869, while the median house price may exceed $1.5 million, reaching $1,621,930.


Market Dynamics and Capital City Variations

However, the report notes variations in capital city performances, attributing a rise in total listings in Melbourne and Sydney to a potential slowdown in price growth. On the flip side, Perth, Brisbane, and Adelaide are expected to benefit from low levels of advertised listings and affordability.


Interest Rate Cuts: Catalyst for Broad Price Growth

Maree Kilroy, the report’s author and Senior Economist at Oxford Economics Australia, emphasizes the potential impact of interest rate cuts from late 2024, which are anticipated to boost credit availability and reignite broad price growth.


Sydney’s Growth Potential Despite Challenges

Specifically addressing Sydney, Kilroy notes a slowing pace of growth attributed to an additional interest rate hike in November and rising total listing volumes. The report predicts house price growth of 3.3% and unit price growth of 5.2% for FY2024.


Government Interventions: Modest Impact on Real Estate

Despite moves by the Albanese Government to curb home price rises, including increased taxes for foreign purchases and doubled vacancy fees for homes owned by overseas investors, the impact on the Sydney real estate market is projected to be modest.


Unit Prices: Affordable Housing Driving Growth

The report suggests that the relatively more affordable price point of units is likely to contribute to stronger growth in the near term. Over the two years to June 2026, Sydney’s median house and unit prices are forecasted to increase by 5.9% and 8.3% per annum, respectively.


Resilience of the Sydney Real Estate Market

While anticipating some impact from government interventions, the report underscores the resilience of the market, citing population growth and a stable interest rate environment as factors likely to support prices in 2024.


In Conclusion: Preparing for Market ShiftsIn conclusion, Sydney’s real estate landscape appears poised for significant shifts, and homeowners and investors are advised to stay informed about the evolving market dynamics.

title: Landmark Palm Beach holiday home lists with an $18m guide
content:
A well-known, vintage holiday home is set to give this year’s Palm Beach record a run for its money with its $18 million price guide and early strong interest.


Rockpool, at 12-14 Rock Bath Rd, has been held for 43 years by the Robertson family and is caught in the 1970s.


However it is on a double block of 1164 sqm with two separate titles and 270 degree views up and down the coast. It is also a property that locals have been watching and waiting for it to come to market.


This is H2 Heading

BJ Edwards, of LH Hooker Palm Beach, said the weekender was well-known in the area and shortly after being listed he had an offer of $17 million.


Currently the top price paid this year in the prestige suburb is $18.7 million for the deepwater trophy home Gaelforce at 995 Barrenjoey Rd, also sold by LJ Hooker Palm Beach.


There are also rumours swirling around that a property has just traded for well over $24 million in Palmie but that has yet to be confirmed.


“Rockpool is set on a massive double block across two separate titles on the south headland of Palm Beach,” Mr Edwards said.


“The views are so phenomenal it feels as though you are on an ocean liner. All three levels enjoy spectacular north-facing views spanning the entire length of Palm Beach to Pittwater and the Central Coast.


“When you walk people through the house you watch their faces and you can see the impact of the view on them, they are all wowed.”


Most of the buyers considering Rockpool want to restore the property as council wouldn’t permit that build again, Mr Edwards said.


There is one buyer interested in replacing the weekender with a substantial house and others looking to separate the titles and sell off or develop them.


Each level is self-contained and there is floor-to-ceiling glass to maximise views. The Robertson family holidayed with the grandparents occupying the top floor, the parents the middle floor and all the grandkids on the lowest level.


In all there are five bedrooms, three bathrooms and parking for five cars.


The tiered level grassy lawns have played host to many a family outdoor movie screening and the property is just steps from the path down to the Palm Beach rockpool and the beach.

title: NSW apartments: New defects insurance scheme to protect off the plan buyers
content:
Dodgy developers and bad builders who construct shoddy apartment towers that can lead to heartbreak and financial ruin for home-buyers are set to be driven out of NSW with a ground-breaking new defects insurance scheme.


In a landmark move by the NSW government, off-the-plan apartment buyers will be offered 10-year insurance against defects in their building and phoenixing developers for the first time in nearly 20 years.


“This is part of a really important journey,” said Gary Dransfield, the past president of the Insurance Council of Australia, who’s just been named the chair of the ministerial advisory panel to hammer out the details of the new system.


“As an interested bystander of the difficulties of the apartment market, I wondered whether the whole program could ever exist. But the government has brought it in and is really committed to this final plank of the program of reforms they have been rolling out through the work of the building commissioner.”


This latest initiative follows years of scandals over buildings like the sinking Mascot Towers near Sydney Airport, the cracking Opal Tower at Sydney Olympic Park, more than 240 apartment blocks with combustible cladding and seemingly new rectification and stop-work orders against developers every week.


Two years ago, building commissioner David Chandler was appointed with unprecedented powers to halt the slide in construction standards in the new apartment industry. His high-profile work has seen developers, building companies and certifiers who carry out defective work slowly being squeezed out.


As the final nail in their coffin, developers will be either invited or ordered – it hasn’t yet been decided – to take out the new decennial liability insurance (DLI) for their towers.

The Redfern house price record has been smashed, with a terrace designed by one of Australia’s most famous architects selling for an extraordinary price.


The Luigi Rosselli-designed residence at 16 Thurlow St had a price guide of $4.5m via Maclay Longhurst of BresicWhitney, but it’s sold for just under $5m.




“The buyer loved the architectural appeal,” says Longhurst. “It really had its own identity.”


He confirmed the purchaser was a young professional woman upgrading from a smaller home in Redfern, though he said “heaps” of young families, priced out of other parts of the east, were now pouncing on bigger homes in the once down-at-heel suburb.


Redfern’s price records are now being broken regularly.


The previous record was $4.65m — set by Longhurst late last month — for a terrace at 108 Buckingham St.


And it’s well known in the Thurlow St neighbourhood that another house has sold for $4.6m recently to a Surry Hills family who have returned from several years working in New York.


No. 16 last traded (pre-renovation) for $1.5m seven years ago.


The buyers (now vendors) of the 5m wide house on the 168 sqm block were Scott Inness and Abby Summerton of Kinn Construction, the builders who often work with Rosselli.


Their stunning designer transformation, completed just two years ago, includes a lower-level rumpus room, home office, laundry and powder room in the basement.


Built over four levels and with its north-facing rear yard, there’s no doubting the property’s architectural credentials.


But some families may have been slightly discouraged by the master bedroom not having an ensuite. And the kitchen, while beautiful, may have been on the smaller side for a family.


It had a garage for one car, with a studio above, accessed via Thurlow Lane.


Longhurst has also just sold 410 Moore Park Rd, Paddington for $9m – a street record and a south Paddington record – in five days.


Owned by lawyer Jason Downing and his director wife Amanda Linott, the guide was $7.5m.

title: Australia’s 5% Deposit Scheme: A Game-Changer for First Home Buyers Starting October 2025
content:
Australia’s housing market has long been a formidable barrier for first-time buyers, with soaring property prices and hefty deposit requirements locking many out of home ownership. In a bold move to address this crisis, the Australian Labor Government has fast-tracked an expanded 5% deposit scheme under the Home Guarantee Scheme, set to launch on 1 October 2025—three months earlier than initially planned. This transformative initiative allows eligible first home buyers to purchase a property with just a 5% deposit, sidestepping the costly Lenders Mortgage Insurance (LMI) that typically accompanies low-deposit loans. With no caps on participant numbers, no income limits, and increased property price thresholds, the scheme promises to open doors for thousands of Australians chasing the dream of owning their first home. This article explores the details, benefits, challenges, and broader implications of this groundbreaking policy.The Housing Affordability Crisis in AustraliaTo understand the significance of the 5% deposit scheme, it’s essential to grasp the scale of Australia’s housing affordability crisis. As of mid-2025, the national median home price stands at approximately $844,000, with regional variations painting an even starker picture. In Sydney, the median house price is around $1.564 million, while Melbourne follows closely at $1.035 million. Even in more affordable cities like Perth ($831,000) or Brisbane ($937,000), the cost of entry remains daunting for first-time buyers.Traditionally, Australian lenders require a 20% deposit to secure a home loan without incurring LMI, a one-off fee designed to protect banks in case of borrower default. For a $844,000 home, a 20% deposit equates to $168,800—a sum that could take the average household 10–12 years to save, assuming they set aside 15% of their gross income annually. For many young Australians, particularly those in their 20s and 30s, this target feels unattainable, especially when grappling with rising rents, cost-of-living pressures, and stagnant wage growth.The Home Guarantee Scheme, first introduced in 2019, sought to address these barriers by allowing the government to act as a guarantor for a portion of the loan, reducing the deposit needed and waiving LMI. The new 5% deposit scheme, launching in October 2025, expands on this framework, making it more accessible and inclusive than ever before.How the 5% Deposit Scheme WorksThe 5% deposit scheme is a cornerstone of the expanded Home Guarantee Scheme, administered by Housing Australia. Under this initiative, first home buyers can purchase a property with a deposit as low as 5%, with the government guaranteeing up to 15% of the loan amount. This eliminates the need for LMI, which can cost anywhere from $10,000 to $40,000 depending on the loan size and lender.Key Features of the Scheme
  • Low Deposit Requirement: Buyers need only a 5% deposit, significantly lowering the upfront savings barrier. For a $700,000 property, this means a deposit of $35,000 instead of $140,000.
  • No LMI: The government’s guarantee removes the need for LMI, saving buyers thousands in additional costs.
  • No Participant Cap: Unlike previous iterations of the scheme, which were limited to a set number of places annually (e.g., 35,000 for the First Home Guarantee), the 2025 expansion has no cap, meaning all eligible applicants can participate.
  • No Income Limits: Earlier versions of the scheme imposed income caps (e.g., $125,000 for singles or $200,000 for couples). The new scheme removes these, broadening eligibility.
  • Higher Property Price Caps: The scheme now accommodates higher property prices, reflecting 2025 market realities. For example, price caps are set at $1.2 million in Sydney, $1 million in Melbourne, and $800,000 in regional areas, ensuring buyers can target realistically priced homes in their desired locations.
  • Eligible Properties: The scheme covers a range of property types, including houses, apartments, townhouses, and house-and-land packages, provided they meet the price cap for the area.
  • Eligibility Criteria: Applicants must be Australian citizens or permanent residents, at least 18 years old, and first-time buyers (or those who haven’t owned property in the past 10 years). They must also intend to live in the purchased property.
Application ProcessTo access the scheme, buyers apply through participating lenders, which include major banks like Commonwealth Bank, NAB, and Westpac, as well as smaller institutions. The lender assesses the applicant’s financial capacity, including income, expenses, and credit history, to ensure they can service the loan. Once approved, Housing Australia provides the guarantee, and the buyer can proceed with their purchase.Benefits for First Home BuyersThe 5% deposit scheme offers several compelling advantages for first-time buyers:1. Lower Barrier to EntryThe most immediate benefit is the reduced deposit requirement. For a $600,000 apartment, a 5% deposit is $30,000—far more achievable than the $120,000 needed for a 20% deposit. This allows buyers to enter the market years earlier, avoiding the need to save for a decade or more while prices continue to rise.2. Savings on LMILMI can be a significant hurdle, often costing tens of thousands of dollars. By eliminating this expense, the scheme reduces the overall cost of purchasing a home, leaving buyers with more funds for other expenses like stamp duty, legal fees, or home furnishings.3. Broader AccessibilityThe removal of income caps and participant limits makes the scheme inclusive for a wider range of buyers, including middle- and high-income earners who may still struggle to save a large deposit. This is particularly impactful for professionals in high-cost cities like Sydney and Melbourne, where even well-paid individuals face affordability challenges.4. Flexibility in Property ChoiceHigher property price caps mean buyers can target homes in desirable areas, rather than being restricted to outer suburbs or regional markets. This flexibility is crucial in 2025, as property prices continue to climb in most capital cities.5. Encouraging Home OwnershipBy making home ownership more attainable, the scheme supports financial security and wealth-building for younger Australians. Property ownership remains a key driver of long-term financial stability in Australia, and this initiative helps bridge the gap for those priced out of the market.Challenges and ConsiderationsWhile the 5% deposit scheme is a significant step forward, it’s not without challenges and potential drawbacks.1. Higher Loan RepaymentsA 5% deposit means a larger loan, which translates to higher monthly repayments and more interest paid over the life of the loan. For example, a $665,000 loan for a $700,000 property (with a 5% deposit) at a 6% interest rate over 30 years results in monthly repayments of approximately $3,990, compared to $3,360 for a $560,000 loan with a 20% deposit. Buyers must ensure they can afford these repayments, especially if interest rates rise.2. Risk of Negative EquityWith a low deposit, buyers have less equity in their home from the outset. If property prices fall, they could owe more on their loan than the property is worth—a situation known as negative equity. While Australia’s property market has historically been resilient, regional variations and economic shifts could pose risks.3. Limited Impact on AffordabilityWhile the scheme lowers the deposit hurdle, it doesn’t address the underlying issue of high property prices. Critics argue that government-backed schemes can inflate demand, potentially pushing prices higher and offsetting affordability gains. The absence of supply-side reforms, such as increasing housing stock or streamlining development approvals, limits the scheme’s long-term impact.4. Financial Discipline RequiredBuyers must demonstrate strong financial discipline to qualify for a loan and manage repayments. Those with high debt levels, irregular incomes, or poor credit histories may struggle to secure approval, even with the government guarantee.5. Regional DisparitiesWhile the scheme’s higher price caps are welcome, they may still fall short in premium suburbs of Sydney and Melbourne, where even modest homes often exceed $1.5 million. Buyers in these areas may need to compromise on location or property type to stay within the caps.Economic and Social ImplicationsThe 5% deposit scheme has far-reaching implications for Australia’s economy and society.Economic StimulusBy enabling more first-time buyers to enter the market, the scheme could stimulate demand for housing, boosting construction, real estate, and related industries. This could create jobs and support economic growth, particularly in regional areas where new developments are common.Wealth InequalityHome ownership is a key driver of wealth accumulation in Australia, with homeowners typically amassing significantly more wealth than renters over time. By helping younger Australians buy homes, the scheme could reduce wealth inequality between generations and socioeconomic groups.Rental Market PressureAs more first-time buyers transition to home ownership, demand for rental properties may decrease, potentially easing pressure on Australia’s tight rental market. This could lead to more stable rents, benefiting those who remain in the rental sector.Political ContextThe scheme is a flagship policy of the Labor Government, reflecting its commitment to addressing housing affordability—a key concern for voters ahead of the 2025 federal election. By fast-tracking the rollout, the government aims to deliver tangible outcomes for young Australians, potentially strengthening its electoral prospects.Comparison with Previous SchemesThe 2025 scheme builds on earlier iterations of the Home Guarantee Scheme, such as the First Home Guarantee (FHG) and the Regional First Home Buyer Guarantee. Previously, the FHG was capped at 35,000 places annually, with income limits of $125,000 for singles and $200,000 for couples. Property price caps were also lower—$900,000 in Sydney and $750,000 in Melbourne—making it harder for buyers in high-cost markets to participate.The new scheme’s removal of participant and income caps, combined with higher price thresholds, makes it far more inclusive. It also aligns with other 2025 housing policies, such as expanded shared equity schemes and increased support for social housing, creating a comprehensive approach to affordability.Case Study: A First-Time Buyer’s JourneyTo illustrate the scheme’s impact, consider Sarah, a 28-year-old teacher earning $85,000 annually in Brisbane. Sarah wants to buy a $600,000 apartment in a suburb like West End. Under traditional lending rules, she’d need a $120,000 deposit (20%) plus LMI, which could cost $15,000–$20,000. Saving this amount would take her 8–10 years, assuming she saves 15% of her income.With the 5% deposit scheme, Sarah needs only $30,000—a target she could realistically achieve in 2–3 years. The government guarantees 15% of her $570,000 loan, waiving LMI. Her monthly repayments, at a 6% interest rate over 30 years, are approximately $3,420. While this is higher than with a larger deposit, it’s manageable on her income, especially with potential tax benefits like the First Home Owner Grant in Queensland.Tips for First-Time BuyersFor those considering the scheme, here are some practical steps:
  • Check Eligibility: Confirm you meet the criteria (e.g., first-time buyer, Australian citizen, owner-occupier).
  • Assess Finances: Use online calculators to estimate repayments and ensure they fit your budget.
  • Shop Around: Compare offers from participating lenders to secure the best loan terms.
  • Research Properties: Look for homes within the price caps for your area, factoring in location and growth potential.
  • Seek Advice: Consult a financial advisor or mortgage broker to navigate the process.
Looking AheadThe 5% deposit scheme is a bold step toward making home ownership more accessible, but it’s not a silver bullet. To truly address affordability, Australia needs a multifaceted approach, including increasing housing supply, reforming tax incentives like negative gearing, and supporting sustainable urban development. As the scheme rolls out in October 2025, its success will depend on effective implementation, lender participation, and broader economic conditions.For first-time buyers, the scheme offers a rare opportunity to break into the property market without the crushing burden of a 20% deposit. While challenges remain, this policy could mark a turning point for a generation locked out of the Great Australian Dream.

The Billionaire’s Formula: Acreage + Austral

There is an old saying in real estate: “Don’t wait to buy land. Buy land and wait.” Nowhere does that ring more true than Austral. Buying acreage here today could be one of the smartest financial moves you will ever make.

  4. Lifestyle Appeal – Acreage offers peace, privacy, and lifestyle flexibility. People crave bigger backyards, room for kids, and even space for businesses or hobby farms. This demand only adds fuel to Austral’s value growth.

Austral is no longer a secret. Savvy buyers—from families to big developers—are rushing to secure land. Here’s why:

  • Affordability (for now): Compared to inner-Sydney suburbs, Austral offers larger blocks at a fraction of the price. But this gap is closing fast.

Austral sits next door to Sydney’s second airport, scheduled to open in just a few years. History shows airports supercharge land values. Look at areas around Kingsford Smith Airport or Brisbane Airport—property prices skyrocketed. The same story is about to play out here, but on an even bigger scale.

Western Sydney Airport is projected to create over 28,000 jobs by 2031 and transform the region into a global business hub. With new jobs comes population growth, housing demand, and—most importantly—soaring land values.

Buying acreage in Austral today is like planting a money tree in the middle of Sydney’s future economic powerhouse.

Stories of Early Investors

Already, families and investors who bought in Austral a decade ago are smiling. Land that once sold for $700,000 an acre is now fetching millions. Subdivision approvals have turned ordinary homeowners into multi-millionaires overnight.

The next wave of investors—those buying today—could become tomorrow’s billionaires.

If you want to join the billionaire club, remember this simple formula:

  • Buy acreage in Austral.
  • Wait for rezoning or subdivision approval.
  • Sell multiple lots or develop.
  • Watch your fortune multiply.

Liverpool, NSW has emerged as one of Sydney's most dynamic and sought-after real estate markets in 2025. Located just 27 kilometres southwest of Sydney's CBD, this historic suburb is experiencing unprecedented growth, attracting first-home buyers, investors, and families seeking value, connectivity, and long-term capital appreciation.




Why Liverpool NSW is Sydney's Property Hotspot in 2025

Record-Breaking Market Performance

Liverpool recorded a median house price of $1,100,000 in Q1 2025, representing annual growth of 10.0% for houses and 8.9% for units. This impressive growth trajectory has positioned Liverpool as a standout performer in the Greater Sydney property market.

The market has demonstrated remarkable resilience throughout 2024 and into 2025. Between Q3 2023 and Q3 2024, Liverpool experienced median house price growth of 13.0%, significantly outpacing many Sydney suburbs. This growth is driven by undersupply in the market, which has created a buffer against higher interest rates.

NSW's #1 Destination for First-Home Buyers

Liverpool has consistently held the top position as NSW's most popular location for first-home buyers. According to InfoTrack's sales data for Q2 of 2025, the Liverpool postcode of 2170 continued to record the highest sales volumes to first home buyers in NSW, marking an entire year the market has held the top ranking.

What's driving this unprecedented demand? Affordability remains Liverpool's strongest drawcard. Buyers can find older-style apartments for around $400,000, which is less than what it costs to build new ones. Recent sales include two-bedroom units selling for $395,000 to $401,000, providing realistic entry points for first-time purchasers.

The suburb is also witnessing a surge in "rentvestors" – first-time buyers who purchase investment properties in Liverpool while continuing to rent closer to the city. These investors are attracted by rental yields around 5% and strong long-term capital growth prospects.

Liverpool's Property Market by the Numbers

Current Median Prices (2025)

  • Houses: $1,100,000 (10% annual growth)
  • Units: $585,000 (8.9% annual growth)

Market Dynamics

Liverpool recorded a vacancy rate of 1.0% in March 2025, which is well below the Real Estate Institute of Australia's healthy benchmark of 3.0%, suggesting quicker occupancy of rental homes. This tight rental market creates excellent conditions for investors seeking consistent rental income.

The market currently favours sellers due to supply constraints. Houses typically spend 39 days on market, while units move even faster at 29 days on average, indicating strong buyer demand across all property types.

Major Infrastructure Transforming Liverpool's Future

Liverpool's property market is being supercharged by billions of dollars in infrastructure investment, positioning the suburb for sustained growth over the coming decades.

Western Sydney International Airport Connection

The upcoming Western Sydney International Airport at Badgerys Creek is a game-changer for Liverpool. To connect residents directly to this new employment and transport hub, governments have committed significant funding to the Fifteenth Avenue Smart Transit (FAST) Corridor.

On 19 January 2025, NSW and Federal governments committed $1 billion to the Fifteenth Avenue Upgrade, with $500 million from the State Government and $500 million from the Federal Government. This corridor will become a direct link to the Bradfield City Centre and the airport, with construction expected to start in 2027.

Major Development Projects

Liverpool City Council released its draft 2025/26 Budget, outlining a $531 million plan to deliver essential services and infrastructure. Some $150 million worth of major projects are being delivered through the Western Sydney Infrastructure Grants Program, including the Carnes Hill Leisure Centre, upgrades to Light Horse Park, and comprehensive upgrades to Macquarie, Scott, and Railway Streets in the Liverpool CBD.

Liverpool Innovation Precinct

The Liverpool Innovation Precinct is anchored by Liverpool Hospital – the largest hospital in NSW and one of Australia's leading trauma centres. This precinct is driving employment growth and attracting healthcare professionals and researchers to the area, creating sustained rental demand.

Educational Investment

Construction has begun on an exciting new project at Liverpool Civic Place that will enable the University of Wollongong to meet the growing demand for university education in the heart of South West Sydney. The university is expanding its Liverpool campus with new courses starting in 2026, including Social Work, Exercise Science, Nutrition Science, and Criminology.

First-Home Buyer's Guide to Liverpool

Buyers are travelling from across Sydney to secure more affordable property in Liverpool, drawn by relative affordability compared to higher-priced suburbs. Many are being priced out of inner suburbs where rents have become unsustainable, making Liverpool a realistic entry point into the property market.

Government Assistance Available

  • First Home Owners Grant (FHOG): $10,000 grant for new homes valued up to $600,000, or house-and-land packages up to $750,000 combined value.
  • Stamp Duty Concessions: Significant savings available for eligible first-home buyers.
  • Help to Buy Scheme: Federal scheme providing shared equity assistance (income caps apply).

  • Rental yield potential if circumstances change

Liverpool's economy is a powerhouse within Western Sydney. Liverpool's growing $16.62 billion economy is larger than 56 nations, with 22,304 registered businesses supporting over 114,501 local jobs.

The Transport, Postal and Warehousing sector is the largest industry, worth $2.3 billion annually, driven by Liverpool's strategic location and logistics infrastructure. The Liverpool Innovation Precinct is fostering growth in healthcare, research, and biotechnology sectors.

  • Liverpool Hospital training facilities

Recreation and Green Space

Liverpool covers 306 square kilometres, of which one third is greenspace with more than 500 open space reserves and 217 sports fields, ovals and courts. Residents enjoy access to numerous parks, recreational facilities, and community amenities.

Market Outlook: What's Next for Liverpool?

Short-Term Outlook (2025-2026)

The market is expected to continue experiencing price growth driven by undersupply and strong demand. While ready-to-sell stock is planned for 2025, it will take time to develop. In the short term, further price growth is expected.

First-home buyer activity will likely remain strong, supported by government incentives and Liverpool's relative affordability compared to other Sydney suburbs.

Long-Term Growth Drivers (2026-2035)

Several major catalysts will drive Liverpool's long-term property market:

  1. Airport Opening: Western Sydney International Airport's opening will create thousands of jobs and increase demand for housing within commuting distance.

  2. FAST Corridor: The Liverpool to Airport Transit Corridor will dramatically improve connectivity, making Liverpool even more attractive to buyers and renters.

  3. Population Growth: With the population expected to exceed 353,000 by 2046, sustained housing demand is virtually guaranteed.

  4. Infrastructure Investment: Billions in infrastructure spending will continue enhancing the suburb's liveability and economic opportunities.

Expert Tips for Buying in Liverpool

For First-Home Buyers

  1. Act Decisively: With Liverpool's strong performance, waiting may mean paying more. Properties are selling quickly, with average market times under 40 days.

  2. Research Suburbs: Each suburb within the Liverpool LGA offers different characteristics. Visit multiple areas to find the best fit for your lifestyle and budget.

  3. Factor in Future Growth: Consider proximity to planned infrastructure like the FAST corridor when choosing your property.

  4. Understand Government Schemes: Ensure you're eligible for and maximizing available grants and concessions.

  5. Get Pre-Approval: In a competitive market, pre-approved buyers have a significant advantage.

For Investors

  2. Consider New Developments: New projects are launching across Liverpool, offering modern amenities and potential for strong capital growth.

  3. Location Matters: Properties near transport, employment hubs, and the university command premium rents and experience lower vacancy.

  4. Long-Term Hold Strategy: Liverpool's fundamentals support a buy-and-hold strategy to maximize capital appreciation as infrastructure is delivered.

  5. Diversify Within the LGA: Consider owning multiple properties across different Liverpool suburbs to spread risk.

Common Questions About Liverpool Real Estate

Major infrastructure including Western Sydney Airport connection ensures long-term capital growth.

Prestons, Moorebank, and parts of Liverpool itself offer family-friendly environments with good schools, parks, and community facilities.

Conclusion: Liverpool's Time is Now

Liverpool, NSW represents one of the most compelling property opportunities in Sydney for 2025 and beyond. Whether you're a first-home buyer seeking affordability, an investor chasing yields and capital growth, or a family looking for space and value, Liverpool delivers.

Buying Property in Sydney as an International Student (2026 Guide)

Quick Answer: Can International Students Buy Property in Sydney?

Yes, international students can buy property in Sydney in 2026, but strict rules apply. Here is what you need to know at a glance:

Who can buy: Temporary visa holders, including student visa holders, classified as foreign persons under Australian law.

Approval required: Most purchases need Foreign Investment Review Board (FIRB) approval before contracts are signed.

What you can buy: Primarily new dwellings and off-plan properties. Buying an established home is only permitted as a primary residence while you are living in Australia, and you must sell it when you leave.

Key costs to budget for: FIRB application fee (from AUD 14,100), stamp duty plus an 8% Foreign Purchaser Duty Surcharge in NSW, legal fees, and a deposit of 20% to 30%.

Best areas: Liverpool NSW, Parramatta, and Western Sydney suburbs offer the most affordable options with strong transport links and growing rental demand.

Next step: Consult a local real estate agent and a property solicitor experienced with international buyers before proceeding.

Can International Students Buy Property in Sydney?

Many international students wonder whether they are legally allowed to purchase property while studying in Australia. The good news is that it is possible, but there are clear rules you must follow.

As a temporary visa holder, including those on a student visa, you are classified as a foreign person under Australian law. This means you are subject to foreign investment regulations governed by the Foreign Investment Review Board (FIRB). Your visa type, your intended use of the property, and the type of dwelling you want to buy all affect what you can and cannot do.

In most cases, student visa holders can only purchase one established dwelling for personal use as their primary residence while they live in Australia. Once you leave the country, you are generally required to sell that property. Purchasing property as an investment while on a student visa is far more restricted, which is why many families choose to buy in the name of a parent or guardian who holds a different visa status.


Buying Property in Sydney as an International Student

Buying property in Sydney as an international student involves several steps that differ from a standard domestic purchase. The process starts with understanding your legal eligibility, then securing FIRB approval before signing any contracts.

Once approval is granted, you will work with a conveyancer or solicitor to handle the legal side of the transaction. You will also need to arrange financing, as not all Australian lenders offer home loans to temporary residents. Having a local real estate agent who understands international buyer property australia requirements makes the entire process significantly smoother.

Key requirements include holding a valid student visa, obtaining FIRB approval where required, purchasing a new or off-plan dwelling in most cases, and having sufficient funds for a deposit, stamp duty, and associated costs.


FIRB Approval Explained

The Foreign Investment Review Board is the Australian government body that reviews and approves property purchases by foreign nationals, including international students. FIRB approval is a legal requirement for most non-citizens and temporary visa holders looking to buy real estate in Australia.

You must apply for FIRB approval before you exchange contracts on a property. Applications are submitted online through the Australian Taxation Office (ATO) portal, and fees are calculated based on the purchase price of the property. For residential properties priced under AUD 1 million, the FIRB application fee starts at AUD 14,100 as of 2026, though you should verify current fees through the official government website.

Processing times vary but typically take 30 days. If your application is not decided within that period, it is generally considered approved. Purchasing a property without FIRB approval when it is required is a serious legal offence and can result in fines or forced sale of the property.


Types of Property You Can Buy

Understanding what kinds of property are available to you as a foreign buyer is essential before you begin your search for sydney property for international buyers.

New dwellings and off-plan properties are the most accessible option. These are properties that have never been lived in, or that are still under construction at the time of purchase. They include newly built apartments, townhouses, and house-and-land packages sold by developers.

Established dwellings are only available to international students under very limited conditions, primarily when purchasing a single property to live in as your main residence while you are studying in Australia. You would typically be required to sell this property once you leave Australia permanently.

Vacant land may also be approved for purchase, provided you commit to building a new dwelling within a specified timeframe.

Commercial property and land for development projects may have separate rules and are worth exploring if your family has a broader investment strategy in mind.


Costs of Buying Property in Sydney

One of the most important things to plan for when considering sydney property for international buyers is the full cost of purchase. Beyond the property price itself, there are several fees and taxes that add up quickly.

Stamp duty is a state government tax applied to the purchase price. In New South Wales, stamp duty on a AUD 700,000 property can be around AUD 26,000 to AUD 28,000 for standard buyers. Foreign purchasers also pay an additional surcharge, known as the Foreign Purchaser Duty Surcharge, which is currently 8% of the purchase price in NSW.

FIRB fees are paid to the government as part of your approval application and are non-refundable regardless of the outcome.

Legal and conveyancing fees typically range from AUD 1,500 to AUD 3,000 depending on the complexity of the transaction.

Mortgage or loan costs include establishment fees, lenders mortgage insurance (LMI) if your deposit is below 20%, and ongoing interest repayments.

Ongoing costs such as strata fees for apartments, council rates, and property management fees should also be factored into your budget.


Best Areas in Sydney for International Students

Choosing the right location is key to getting value from your investment. Several suburbs offer a good balance of affordability, connectivity, and lifestyle for international students studying in Sydney.

Liverpool NSW is one of the most attractive options for international student property australia buyers. It sits in Sydney's southwest and offers significantly lower property prices compared to inner-city suburbs. Liverpool has excellent transport links to the Sydney CBD and is close to Western Sydney University and other institutions. The area has a culturally diverse population, a growing local economy, and strong rental demand, making it a smart place to start your search. You can browse real estate in Liverpool to get a feel for what is available in the market.

Parramatta is another popular choice, sitting roughly 23 kilometres west of the CBD. It is home to Western Sydney University and offers good bus and train connections. Property prices are more affordable than the eastern suburbs while still providing access to a full range of amenities.

Blacktown, Penrith, and Campbelltown are further west and offer some of the most affordable entry points into the Sydney market, with new housing estates and apartment developments catering to first-time buyers and investors alike.

Inner suburbs such as Haymarket, Ultimo, and Chippendale attract students who want to be close to the University of Sydney and UTS, though prices in these areas are considerably higher.


Financing Options for International Students

Securing a home loan as a temporary resident in Australia can be more challenging than it is for Australian citizens or permanent residents. Not all banks and lenders offer loans to student visa holders, and those that do often apply stricter conditions.

Most lenders will require a deposit of at least 20% to 30% of the purchase price. Some may require more, particularly if you have limited Australian income history. If your income comes from overseas, it may be discounted when the lender assesses your borrowing capacity.

Specialist mortgage brokers who work with international clients can help you identify lenders that are experienced with foreign income and non-resident applications. It is worth comparing multiple options before committing to a lender, as interest rates and loan conditions vary widely.

If you are purchasing as part of a family arrangement, having a co-borrower who is an Australian resident can sometimes improve your loan eligibility. Always seek independent financial advice before making any borrowing decisions.


Risks and Challenges to Consider

Like any property purchase, buying as an international student involves risks that are worth understanding before you commit.

Legal complexity is one of the biggest challenges. Foreign investment property australia regulations are detailed and change over time. Getting them wrong, such as buying without FIRB approval or purchasing the wrong type of property, can result in significant financial and legal penalties.

Currency exchange risk affects buyers who are converting money from an overseas currency to Australian dollars. Fluctuations in exchange rates can make your purchase more expensive than expected and affect your ability to service a loan.

Market fluctuations are another factor. Sydney property prices can rise and fall based on economic conditions, interest rates, and government policy. There is no guarantee that a property purchased today will increase in value over the short term.

Visa changes can also affect your plans. If your visa status changes or you are required to leave Australia, you may need to sell the property under conditions that are not favourable.


Why Liverpool NSW Is a Smart Choice

For international students and their families exploring affordable and well-connected options, Liverpool NSW consistently stands out as a strategic investment location.

Property prices in Liverpool remain well below the Sydney metro average, meaning you can enter the market at a lower price point while still having access to all the infrastructure of a major city. The suburb is serviced by the T2 South train line, providing direct access to the Sydney CBD in under an hour. The Western Sydney Airport, currently under development at Badgerys Creek, is set to further boost property values in the surrounding areas over the coming years.

Liverpool also has a large population of international students and a strong multicultural community, which means services, groceries, restaurants, and community support networks are well established for newcomers.

Stamp Duty and Government Charges

Stamp duty is one of the largest additional costs of buying property in Australia, and it is charged by the NSW state government based on the purchase price of the property. For a property valued at $800,000, stamp duty in NSW can exceed $31,000. This must typically be paid at or before settlement.

In addition to stamp duty, buyers also pay transfer fees and property registration fees. These NSW property buying fees are processed through the NSW Land Registry Services and cover the formal transfer of ownership from the seller to the buyer.

First home buyers may be eligible for relief through the NSW First Home Buyer Assistance Scheme, which provides full or partial exemptions from stamp duty for eligible properties. Buyers are encouraged to check their eligibility through the NSW Revenue Office before settlement to understand what financial support may be available.


Building and Pest Inspection Costs

A building and pest inspection is a critical step when buying property in Western Sydney or anywhere across NSW. These inspections are conducted before purchase to identify structural problems, moisture issues, termite activity, and other defects that may not be visible during a standard property viewing.

The cost of a combined building and pest inspection in NSW typically ranges from $400 to $700 depending on the size and location of the property. While this may feel like an additional burden, it is a small amount compared to the cost of unexpected repairs after settlement.

Mortgage and Loan Related Expenses

When budgeting for first home buyer costs in NSW, it is important not to overlook the fees associated with obtaining a home loan. Many lenders charge an application or establishment fee that can range from $200 to $700. Valuation fees, which cover the lender's assessment of the property's market value, can add a further $200 to $500.

Buyers who borrow more than 80 percent of a property's value will also be required to pay Lenders Mortgage Insurance, commonly known as LMI. This is a one-off premium that protects the lender, not the borrower, and can range from a few thousand dollars to well above $10,000 depending on the loan amount.

Ongoing loan charges such as annual fees, offset account fees, and redraw fees should also be reviewed carefully before choosing a lender. Comparing home loan products thoroughly can help buyers reduce these long-term expenses.
